Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. I found no blocking items.

The post refuses positive G84 and G85 dwell requests by name. It suppresses the refused hole's expanded cuts. Zero-dwell cycles still post.

I checked the laws in upstream/main:AGENTS.md at `3e47b898b0148727979ff4a509f33a742f80ff1d`.
The change meets issue #2357. The issue permits a named G84 refusal.
[Siemens table 6-2](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf#page=97) lists P for G84 and no P for G85.
The G84 message states the post's limitation.

Local checks:

- The trial merge with upstream/main was clean. The PR already contains that main commit.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS, 46 steps, 312 tests, no failures or ignored tests.
- The gate built the selected post and app test targets with `cargo test --no-run`.
- `RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: PASS.

Mutation checks that I ran locally:

1. Restore the upstream post: RED. Both positive-dwell tests fail because the named refusal is absent. The zero-dwell test passes.
2. Remove the refused-hole tracking: RED. Both refusal tests fail because G1 cuts reach the output. The zero-dwell test passes.
3. Restore the PR post: GREEN. All three regression tests pass.

The mutations were temporary. The working tree is clean after restoration.
The tests cover 1 ms, 250 ms, and a hand-written fractional millisecond.

Golden files: none changed. No moved golden lines require inspection.
UI: no changes. Screenshots are not required.
No physical controller was tested. G84 dwell output remains unsupported by this post.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
